text:
incident-bot: PAGING ALERT: high paging + model-warmup failures in eu-west-1 (pool: rt-eu-*). Symptoms: GPU hangs / driver panics, repeated deserialization OOMs, container restart loops. Trigger detected 02:14:12 UTC.

maya: seeing a sharp spike in page_faults and mmap faulting during artifact load. Several pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff with SIGBUS while reading mmaped shards.

oscar: sample pod log: ```
[2026-03-15T02:14:12Z] model_loader: mmap artifact /artifacts/gpt-xl-v1.q4_0 size=3.2G
[2026-03-15T02:14:14Z] cuda: cuCtxCreate failed: 701 (cuda driver hang)
[2026-03-15T02:14:16Z] compile: kernel compile timed out after 45s
[2026-03-15T02:14:17Z] runtime: failed to allocate KV cache 2.0G (oom)
[2026-03-15T02:14:17Z] kernel: SIGBUS at 0x7f8a1c2b0000
[2026-03-15T02:14:18Z] process: container terminated (OOM/Crash)
```

rachel: node telemetry shows node-11 and node-14 with repeated NVML resets; kubelet restarted on node-14 at 02:15:03. memory.available on node-11 drifted from 6GB to 300MB in ~20s.

toni: this looks like a combined behavior: artifact deserializer holding pages + JIT compile storm + driver instability under pressure. When mmap-backed pages fault into RAM during compile, driver memory spikes then NVML resets.

ev an: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) cordon node-11 and node-14, 2) reduce warmup concurrency (env WARMUP_PARALLEL=1) for rt-eu pool, 3) set PRECOMPILE_KERNELS=1 to avoid runtime JIT, 4) disable eager prefetch for large q4/q8 artifacts, 5) route non-critical tenants to fallback quantized-small models.

carina: customer-impact check: five enterprise tenants report 5xx errors; overall generate error-rate up +19% in last 10m, p95 latency moved 0.9s -> 3.8s. Dedicated customers on eu-west-1 showing retries and longer tail latencies.

oscar: I'm cordoning node-11 and node-14 now and draining non-critical pods. Marking them unschedulable.

maya: toggled PRECOMPILE_KERNELS=1 on eu-west-1 runtime pool; patching rollout to 20% first. Also flagging service route to failover to eu-central for lower tier traffic.

incident-bot: oncall-handoff scheduled: maya -> oscar at 02:30 UTC. If severity increases, escalate to #eng-oncall.

toni: pushed a conservative deserializer change to call madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) on large tensor pages after load. Canarying on 2 pods. This should lower RSS and reduce page-in spikes.

eoscar: applied temporary rate limiter for warmup endpoints to 10 req/s to avoid warmup stampede. Also disabled eager prefetch for artifacts >1.5G. Monitoring.

rachel: early signal: compile_timeouts fell from 24/min -> 4/min on nodes with PRECOMPILE_KERNELS, RSS on canary pods down ~700MB after madvise patch. error-rate fell to ~8% in last 5m.

carina: customer comms update sent to affected tenants: "We're investigating transient 5xx and high latency; mitigation in progress; expected restoration in 30-90 minutes. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary." They acknowledged.

maya: we should consider temporary rollback of last week's GPU driver update on eu-west-1 nodes; the timing correlates with driver changes. Jim (runtime) please verify driver logs; Toni please correlate compile allocator allocations.

toni: collecting allocator traces and will upload to the ticket. Preliminary shows larger pinned allocations during JIT compile. madvise helps but driver behavior may be primary.

eoscar: cordon/drain done for node-11/14. Re-sched attempts hitting warmup throttles which is good. Keeping 1 replica buffer for the pool to avoid mass cold starts.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied: node cordons, precompile kernels enabled, warmup concurrency reduced, eager prefetch disabled, deserializer madvise canary, temporary warmup rate-limit. Error rate down to 7% last 5m.

rachel: plan after initial stabilization: 1) leave nodes cordoned until driver stability confirmed and kubelet uptime > 30m, 2) rollback driver if diagnostics point to regression, 3) add an alert for mmap_fails/mmaps_pageins spike and for compile_timeouts > 5/min, 4) add a safety valve: cap parallel JIT compiles to 1 per node.

carina: note for postmortem: affected customers want SLO impact numbers and timeline. I'll compile generation error count per tenant and attach to incident ticket.

oscar: handing off next watch to rachel in 20m. rachel will be primary for followups and postmortem.

maya: checklist for post-incident: reproduce in staging with driver pinned, add e2e test for madvise correctness under heavy parallel deserial, add telemetry for mmap churn, schedule driver A/B test for next upgrade.

toni: also adding defensive change: on deserializer failure, proactively fall back to streaming-from-blob (avoid big mmap) to prevent SIGBUS.

carina: customers acknowledged mitigations. We'll propose a postmortem and target actions to close.

oscar: closing loop: I'll attach GPU dmesg, nvpe logs, and pod IDs to the incident ticket (pods: rt-eu-2f7, rt-eu-9d4, rt-eu-0b1). Timeline: detection 02:14 UTC, mitigations by 02:28 UTC, partial recovery 02:42 UTC.

rachel: thanks team, great coordination. Will keep monitoring for 1h and will open a SEV-2 postmortem doc. Ping #eng-oncall if any regressions. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: HANDOFF: maya -> oscar at 02:30 UTC (automated).
